title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 66-68): Grothendieck works with 'disjonctions' or 'dispositions'. A disposition is a set E with a relation x|0|y ('disjoint', 'incompatible'). From it he builds Σ_E, a complete lattice of distinguished subsets of E: 'closed', saturated or 'Vic°'-type sets. In Σ_E the Sup is not in general the union but a closure of the union. On p.66 he computed when a correspondence α:E→E' has a 'transpose' β:E'→E, described through supports and cosupports.

This page restarts the definition. He first drafts and crosses out: a pair (α_*,β_*) of maps Σ_E→Σ_E', Σ_E'→Σ_E. He then settles on a different definition. A 'correspondance dispositionnelle' from E to E' is a map α_*:Σ_E→Σ_E' commuting with arbitrary Sups, possibly together with a transpose.

The motivation is the trivial case. A relation α⊂E×E' is the same thing as a union-preserving map P(E)→P(E'); the margin note reads 'correspondances comme applications de P(E)'. Sup-preserving maps between the lattices Σ_E therefore generalize relations of 'trivial dispositions', where Σ_E=P(E).

He then claims that such an α_* is determined by a plain map α:E→Σ_E', x ↦ α_*(Sup Vic°_E({x})), the image of the 'point-closure' of x. Conversely, on p.68 he extends a given α by α_*(S)=Sup_{x∈S} α(x) = s-η°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)). This gives the claimed 'Lemme': a bijection Hom_Ens(E,Σ_E') ≅ Hom_ord^!(Σ_E,Σ_E'), the order maps preserving all Sups.

Next he wants a transpose generalizing x'∈α(x) ⇔ x∈β(x'). He writes it through negations: x'|0|α(x) ⇔ x|0|β(x'). This is a polarity/Galois-type adjunction for orthogonality relations.

In modern terms: the category of sup-lattices, viewed as a generalization of the category Rel of sets and relations (the Joyal–Tierney viewpoint). Σ_E is the lattice of closed sets of an orthogonality/closure space, and the transpose is an adjoint taken through the orthocomplement, as in Chu-space or Foulis–Randall duality. The page is an exploratory set-up of foundational definitions.
errors: The bijection Hom_Ens(E,Σ_E') ≅ Hom_sup(Σ_E,Σ_E') holds only when every element of Σ_E is the Sup of point-closures and E→Σ_E is a free sup-generator. That is the case for trivial dispositions, Σ_E=P(E).

In general a function α:E→Σ_E' extends to a Sup-preserving map only if it respects the closure: x∈cl(S) ⇒ α(x) ≤ Sup_{y∈S} α(y). Otherwise α_*(S)=Sup_{x∈S}α(x) is not well defined on closed sets, or is not Sup-preserving.
Grothendieck himself flags the issue in the margin of p.68 ('il n'est pas clair que si A⊂E fermé, α_*(A) soit fermé'). So the 'Lemme' as stated needs this extra continuity hypothesis.
The transposition via negations requires a symmetry/separation property of |0| (noted in the NB of p.66). Without it, β need not exist or be unique.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine foundational set-up: sup-lattice morphisms generalizing relations, plus a transpose through an orthogonality relation. It is standard order theory and Chu-space style duality, and the stated lemma is even incorrect without a continuity hypothesis. It is of mild interest only as evidence of Grothendieck's 1986 work on 'dispositions/disjonctions'.
transcription_corrections: The margin note, written diagonally, likely reads 'Correspondances comme applications de 𝔓(E) [commutant aux ∪]'. It is attached to the P(E) discussion, not a separate statement.
The crossed-out text after 's'il' reads approximately 'existe une application β_*: Σ_{E'} ...'; the replacement is 'elle commute aux Sup quelconques'.
The point-closure in the definition of α(x) is Sup Vic°_E({x}), with S(x) subscripted beneath. It denotes the smallest element of Σ_E containing x.
